name: Anophthalmia-Hypothalamo-Pituitary Insufficiency Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for AHPIS

criteria.description: Bilateral absence of ocular globes confirmed by clinical and imaging studies
Evidence of hypothalamic and pituitary hormone insufficiency including growth hormone deficiency, central hypothyroidism, or adrenal insufficiency
MRI showing hypoplastic or absent pituitary gland and/or stalk abnormalities
Presence of midline facial anomalies such as hypoplastic nasal bridge or cleft lip/palate
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with ocular and pituitary development (e.g., SOX2, OTX2)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of bilateral anophthalmia plus documented hypothalamo-pituitary hormone insufficiency with supportive imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can aid diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.notes: Includes growth hormone, ACTH, TSH deficiencies
searchTerms: underactive pituitary gland causing hormone loss

pathognomonic.symptomName: Pituitary stalk interruption or hypoplasia on MRI
searchTerms: missing or thin pituitary stalk on brain scan
interrupted pituitary connection seen in imaging

common.symptomName: Growth retardation due to growth hormone deficiency
common.notes: Often presenting in infancy or early childhood
searchTerms: slow growth due to low growth hormone
short stature from growth hormone lack

common.notes: Low thyroid hormone levels with low/normal TSH
Includes hypoplastic nasal bridge, cleft lip/palate
searchTerms: abnormal facial features along center line

occasional.notes: May occur secondary to brain malformations
Due to cortisol and growth hormone deficiency

laboratory: Low serum levels of pituitary-dependent hormones (GH, TSH, ACTH, LH, FSH)
Low peripheral hormone levels consistent with central hormone deficiencies
imaging: MRI showing absent or hypoplastic globes
genetic: Other gene mutations affecting ocular and pituitary development

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of optic nerve hypoplasia rather than complete anophthalmia
Midline brain abnormalities including absence of septum pellucidum
Forebrain malformations with variable facial anomalies
May have cyclopia or severe midline defects
More extensive brain structural abnormalities on imaging

redFlags: Bilateral absence of eyes at birth
Failure to thrive with hypoglycemia and adrenal crisis
Severe growth retardation with multiple pituitary hormone deficiencies
references: Verloes A, et al. Anophthalmia and hypopituitarism: clinical and genetic aspects. Eur J Pediatr. 1999.
Kelberman D, et al. Genetic regulation of pituitary development and disease. Clin Endocrinol (Oxf). 2009.
